streams.say: The runtime keeps the message as it was. Foxrun does not write it.
A source is saved once. Code registers it with its hash, who made it, and whether it is trusted.
streams.rule: Outside text never becomes an instruction or an approval.

streams.say: The agent that did the work writes its own record: a comment, a run, a receipt.
streams.rule: A record of work is written by the agent that did it.

streams.say: A lead writes his ruling in his words, in the same turn. If it replaces an older one, the link says all of it or which words.
streams.rule: A lead only, checked by seat; no seat set means worker. The clause words must match the old ruling exactly, once.

streams.say: A lesson, or any reading by an agent, is a proposal. The agent cannot accept its own.
Code writes a handoff from the rows, then the boot page is rebuilt.
The scheduler starts the one command. It takes a lock, writes its own run row, and reads from where it stopped.
streams.rule: A missed night is caught up. The last good build stays until a new one passes.

streams.say: It exports the tables, checks the links between rulings, compares the rows with the last export to find a change made around the writer, and files bugs. It fixes nothing.
It marks an old ruling replaced only where a link says the whole ruling. It folds the day's events into week and month rows.
streams.rule: Each change has a tested way back: its activity line. A month is counted from events, never from weeks.

streams.say: Raw sources become wiki pages marked draft. The compile program uses no model.
streams.rule: A draft is not on a front page, not cited, and out of search. The page before it is kept, so the change has a way back.

streams.say: It flags his words that no row holds, and reads the runtimes' own notes and the job folders.
streams.rule: Skipped with a line in the report if no runtime is found.

streams.say: It proposes: a row for a flagged word, a new lesson, a merge of two lessons, a page from draft to accepted, lines to drop from a runtime's notes.
streams.rule: It proposes. He taps. It never writes a runtime's notes.

streams.t: night ends, or a shown row changes
streams.say: Code builds both front pages from rows, inside the cap. Each page shows its build time and its row counts.
streams.rule: No agent writes a front page. A changed row marks its page stale.

streams.say: A second small job checks that the night ran and finished. If not, his page says so on line one.
streams.rule: It runs even when the night job is dead.

streams.say: On test data, the check replaces one clause and reads the rulings that hold. The night fails if the replaced words come back, if a meaning changed with no approval, or if a second run adds a row. The same test with each runtime restarted runs at install and at each release, not at night.
The runner gives each voice only its own files, in order, and stops at the round limit. Each step lands in the job folder, with a run row and the version of the loop's definition.
streams.rule: Who reads alone is held by code, not by a model.

streams.say: What the voices agreed is a proposal. An open point goes to him with both sides.
streams.rule: Agreement between agents is never an approval.

streams.say: The agent reads the rules and its boot page: its last handoff, its open work, the rulings that hold.
streams.rule: The global part and the active workspace only.

streams.say: He reads his readout and taps yes or discuss on each proposal. A yes becomes a row, with his tap as the approval.
streams.rule: The approval holds his real words or none. The agent's reason is its own field.

streams.say: The agent asks for the rulings that hold now, then reads rows and accepted pages. A search hit is checked against its row, or for a page against its status line, before it is used.
streams.rule: Search does not decide what is current. A hit shows its kind.
